findings.note: ESPN lists Freddy Peralta for TB (1.93 ERA in 4.2 postseason IP) against Cleveland LHP Parker Messick (5.40 ERA, 6 BB in 6.2 IP) for ALCS Game 2. Cleveland leads the series 1-0, ESPN's predictor gives TB 59.5%, the listed TB moneyline is -137, and Shane McClanahan is marked OUT.

Cleveland came back from 2-0 down to win Game 1 7-3, scoring all seven runs in the last four innings, and has now won four straight. The Rays managed only three runs from seven hits and two walks. CBS also says Cleveland's pitching staff was compromised after its five-game division series.

Cleveland had 14 hits and hit two homers off Rays ace Drew Rasmussen. José Ramírez went 3-for-5 and Vogt says he keeps feeling better after his hamate surgery. Midseason pickups Lowe and Adell also drove in runs, so Cleveland's offense looks better than its season stats.

Cleveland starter Parker Messick has a 5.40 ERA, 1.80 WHIP and 6 walks in 6.2 postseason innings, facing Freddy Peralta (1.93 ERA). ESPN lists the total at 7, so 6.5 is half a run under it. The game is at Tropicana Field, so weather shouldn't matter.

Game 1 ended 7-3 (10 runs), with Cleveland scoring seven in the last four innings. CBS says Cleveland's pitching was compromised after a five-game ALDS. On the other side, Tampa's staff allowed only five runs in 27 innings against the Yankees.
CBS links an article headlined 'Offense at historic low in MLB playoffs,' which points to low scoring league-wide this postseason. It's general context and isn't specific to this game.

MLB.com's ALCS Game 2 preview has Caminero batting third at 3B and says he and DeLuca reported feeling fine after their Game 1 collision. It also notes the Rays' bats have been quiet and Caminero hasn't had a real 'moment' yet this postseason.

Game 1 box score: Caminero went 1-for-4 with only a single and struck out twice against Cleveland's bullpen (Espino, Gaddis). His postseason slash line is .286/.375/.357, which points to little extra-base damage so far.

CBS Sports says Caminero hit just .182 with no homers and two RBI against Cleveland in the 5-1 regular-season series, though it also notes he finished second in the AL with 42 regular-season home runs.

MLB.com's Game 2 preview says Messick's two ALDS starts were short (4 1/3 IP, then 2 1/3 IP on 65 pitches with four walks), and with Wednesday off the Guardians could have a full bullpen ready, which points to a short outing; the preview also expects Austin Hedges to catch him.

Confirms Messick starts Game 2 on normal rest and is already at 193 IP, well past his previous career high of 138 1/3, which raises a fatigue question; however, he says he feels great and his four-seam velocity in his last start (95.6 mph) was above his season average.

Messick struck out nine Rays in 5 2/3 innings on April 27, 2026, and also struck out six of them over 7 2/3 innings on July 26, so he has gone over 4.5 strikeouts in both 2026 starts against Tampa Bay.

Confirms Messick starts ALCS Game 2 but says his two ALDS starts were short (4 1/3 IP, then 2 1/3 IP and 65 pitches with four walks), and Wednesday's off day gives Vogt a full, rested bullpen, which points to a short leash.

Says Messick is at 193 innings this season, far above his previous career high of 138 1/3, so fatigue is a risk; he says he feels great and his fastball velocity in his last start was above his season average.

In his July 26 start against the Rays at Tropicana Field, Messick struck out six over 7 2/3 innings with no walks and was 2-0 with a 1.03 ERA in four career starts against Tampa Bay; MLB video also shows a nine-strikeout start against them in April.
